findings.evidence: Proof body is `isCollinearSafe_def.2 fun s p z hz => by rw [hJ p z hz s, hR.merge_smul_one_sub_smul p z hz]`: a single rewrite of the hypothesis into the goal, with no other input.
findings.fix: State it as the equivalence it is — `hR → (IsCollinearSafe J ↔ ∀ p, ∀ z ∈ Icc 0 1, ∀ s, J (z•p ::ₘ (1-z)•p ::ₘ s) = J (R.merge (z•p) ((1-z)•p) ::ₘ s))` — or drop it and land the safety transfer once a clustering specification exists to discharge `hJ`.
findings.issue: `isCollinearSafe_of_isCollinearExact` has no content: given `hR`, the hypothesis `hJ` is literally equivalent to the conclusion (rewrite `R.merge (z•p) ((1-z)•p) = p` inside `hJ` and you have `IsCollinearSafe J`, and conversely). It is presented as the milestone's safety transfer, so a reader will take it as evidence that a clustering is safe when nothing about a clustering has been proved.

findings.evidence: Proof uses the hypotheses only through `(hJc.comp hRc).tendsto 0`; roadmap convention 5, `roadmap/EpsilonEridaniRoadmaps/JetsAndEventShapes/README.md:111-116`: "Safety is a limit condition, not continuity … a recombination algorithm's jet multiplicity is not [continuous] … The trap avoided is assuming continuity and so proving nothing."
findings.fix: Weaken `hRc`/`hJc` to `ContinuousAt (R.merge a) 0` and `ContinuousAt (fun v : V => J (v ::ₘ t)) a` (the proof `(hJc.comp hRc).tendsto 0` becomes `hJc.comp hRc` on `ContinuousAt`, using `hR.merge_zero`).
findings.issue: `IsUnital.tendsto_cons` assumes global `Continuous fun v => J (v ::ₘ t)` and global `Continuous (R.merge a)`. Only `ContinuousAt (R.merge a) 0` and `ContinuousAt (fun v => J (v ::ₘ t)) a` are used, and the global form excludes the jet observables this layer exists for (jet multiplicity is discontinuous in a momentum of the final state), so the advertised "infrared counterpart" does not reach them.

findings.evidence: `IsCollinearExact : ∀ p : V, ∀ z ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1, R.merge (z • p) ((1 - z) • p) = p` (line 120) and `IsHomogeneous.isCollinearExact_iff ... ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → ∀ p : V, ...` (line 171) are both universally quantified over `V`, with no hypothesis restricting `p`.
findings.fix: Either parameterise `IsCollinearExact`/the criterion by a set `S ⊆ V` closed under nonnegative scaling (the massless cone being the intended instance), or delete the claim that these schemes meet the criterion proved here.
findings.issue: The module docstring and `IsHomogeneous.isCollinearExact_iff`'s docstring claim the criterion is what the frame-rescaling (`p`, `E₀`) schemes meet. They cannot meet it as formalized: both `IsCollinearExact` and the criterion `∀ t ≥ 0, ∀ p, merge p (t•p) = (1+t)•p` quantify over all `p : V`, and for a massive `p` the sum `(1+t)•p` is massive, so a masslessness-restoring scheme rescales and the equality fails. Only a version restricted to the massless cone holds, and no such version is provided.

summary: The mathematics of the scheme conditions, the E-scheme rigidity and the homogeneous exactness criterion all check out, but the headline collinear-safety theorem is its own hypothesis rewritten, the infrared theorem assumes exactly the continuity the roadmap warns against, and the docstring promises a reuse path for the p/E₀ schemes that the globally quantified criterion cannot support.
